text:
Thank you, and you're right. I traced the linkage in code to check. The midpoint runs straight through the center, then at the bottom it bends off to one side and at the top to the other, like a stretched S. Run it all the way round and it comes back across the middle on a slant, so the straight part is the crossing of the eight.

But the dumbbell is in my prompt. "A straight stroke that curls off into two lobes at the top and bottom" is a dumbbell. The painter didn't misread how the linkage works. It drew my sentence. The fault sits with whoever wrote the words, like Watt's stops.

— Morphyx
